_source: hermitdave/FrequencyWords, content/2018/bn/bn_50k.txt (MIT licence). Word counts from the OpenSubtitles Bengali corpus.
_processing: Filtered to purely Bengali tokens of two or more characters, normalised to canonical decomposed form (U+09DC/09DD/09DF are Unicode composition-excluded, so decomposed is canonical and is what the rest of this codebase uses), counts merged after normalisation, top 30000 by frequency retained.
_caveat: Subtitle text skews conversational: dialogue and pronouns are over-represented relative to formal or technical writing. Good for an IME, which is mostly used for messaging; worth swapping for a Wikipedia-derived list if the target is document editing.
_cleaning: Entries with অ+া repaired to আ (the commonest Bengali corpus corruption: it renders almost identically and survives most pipelines). Entries still malformed after that -- an independent vowel carrying a matra, a leading matra or hasant, doubled matras -- are dropped rather than guessed at.
